Cameroun Citoyen

An independent civic guide to Cameroon: compare the written positions of the parties, read election results with their sources, explore history and the ten regions, and find who is responsible for what near home.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Information on Cameroonian parties, elections and institutions is scattered across party sites, news reports and archives, often without a date or a source. Voters end up choosing on reputation rather than on written positions, and few people know which official answers for a broken water point in their street.

02

What it does

A 24-question citizen profile matched against the written positions of 14 parties, with agreements, disagreements and topics still undocumented; party files and a side-by-side comparison of up to three; proclaimed election results with registered voters, valid votes and turnout, kept apart from the contestations; a history timeline from 1884; a 3D atlas of the ten regions; a constituency page with the role of each official and a letter to prepare; short courses; books and essays to read in full; a source library; and daily headlines from Cameroonian and international newsrooms.

03

How it is built

React, with Three.js for the regions atlas and PDF.js to convert documents in the browser. Every entry carries its source and date, and percentages are reproduced as published. The questionnaire can be saved and resumed; no party receives the answers, and origin, religion and region are never used. For the law itself, the sidebar links to Droit Facile.
